title: Project layout and imports

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
A clear project layout helps imports and collaboration; avoid naming a local module after a standard-library module.
CORE EXPLANATION
Separating modules, tests, and data makes even a small project easier to grow. Avoid filenames that shadow standard-library modules, and test package execution with python -m.
EXAMPLE CODE
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

project = PurePosixPath('project')
files = ('pyproject.toml', 'src/app/__init__.py', 'tests/test_app.py')
for file in files:
    print(project / file)

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Do not name a project file after an imported module; Python may import that file instead.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: Do not remove the operating system's Python or install packages globally without a reason.
COMMON MISTAKES
Keep the interpreter, pip, and project packages in the same virtual environment.
